chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from 'Illan from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the woman who menstruates once every three months, or in a year, or in seven months, and the istihadah (continuous bleeding) woman, and the one who has not yet reached puberty, and the one who menstruates once and then stops once, and the one who does not hope for children, and the one whose menstruation has ceased but claims she has not despaired (of it returning), and the one who sees the white discharge from menstruation which is not regular, he mentioned that the waiting period ('iddah) for all of these is three months.

key_terms.الصَّفْرَةَ: White discharge (often associated with the end of menses)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: Woman with istihadah (continuous uterine bleeding outside of regular menses)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman with irregular or absent menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar establishes a three-month 'iddah for women with irregular or absent menstruation, serving as a practical legal default when the standard 'iddah based on cycles or pregnancy cannot be applied. It reflects the Shia juristic approach to resolving ambiguity in menstrual status by setting a fixed temporal period for purification and remarriage eligibility.
